items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: The mention of Sidney Bichet occurs in a turn by the [INTERVIEWER] ('He used to play with Sidney Bichet... They played with Sidney Bichet'). The interviewee (Lee Collins) does not mention Sidney Bichet in his own turns, nor does he respond to the interviewer's mention of Bichet with any personal ane

ctx.x: Oh, I just woke the man, I told him, I said, man, I've been buying your magazine for 15 years. I said, please, I actually have a special favor. Please print this letter for me. Mr. Mouse. Man, the boy I drug with. I sure hope he puts it up. He pointed me up, you know what I mean. I just hate to see a man talk that way about another man. You know what I mean. You don't have to talk that way about him.

When he tried to copy, he stole his jelly piece of him and he was a finger buster. He couldn't even play it. He put his name down and composed it. He used to play with Sidney Bichet. I don't know how to really hurt him, I guess, in New York, out on Long Island. They played with Sidney Bichet. I don't know who else. I don't know. Maybe.

I put one line in there. It got a part in there about they didn't know how to wear their pegs. I told him, I said, in the joints in Storyville where Janice sat and played, I said, you couldn't even come in the joint because they didn't find out how much lying you was. Did you ever hear him play down here at all? No, no. See, before he died, about eight months before he died, I lived with him and his wife for nine months in New York. I never knew him before, but when I went to New York, I made a point in my mind…
